title: The claim sync and the close commit of a host project are pushed by a backlog.py command, not by hand (second-project run)
goal: A host project pushes its claim commits and its close commit with a backlog.py command that runs land_push (the skill names it), since close deletes the items land needs and a hand push is denied to agents

run:
import argparse, sys
sys.path.insert(0, "_tools")
import backlog, bl_cli
ap = bl_cli.build_parser("x", ".")
sub = next(a for a in ap._actions if isinstance(a, argparse._SubParsersAction))
hits = [n for n, p in sub.choices.items() if "land_push" in " ".join(p.format_help().split())]
assert hits, "no backlog.py command or option is documented as running the project land_push"

notes: Run findings 21 and 27: the skill tells the orchestrator to push the claims with land_push's argv by hand (git push denied); land ST-... --branch main after close --commit: no item ST-...: its file was deleted (a closed sprint's item); the close commit stayed local.
